sentences.text: 3. Heard finally with the consent of the learned Counsel for the applicant and learned counsel for the respondent.
Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt 4.

By this revision application, the applicant challenges the judgment and order of maintenance passed in Petition E- 13/2021 by which Family Court, Yavatmal granted maintenance at the rate of Rs.2,000/- to the wife and the Rs.2,000/- to the son.
5. The marriage between the applicant and the respondent wife was solemnized as per Hindu rites and customs at Yavatmal on 19.11.2019.
Out of said wedlock, one son was born on 26.08.2020.
As per the allegation of the respondent that after marriage, she resided with him and his mother in matrimonial home at Nagpur.
His two sisters are married and staying at their matrimonial house along with their husband.
Prior to the marriage, she was serving and the applicant was serving in Anchor Company at Nagpur.

It is alleged that since beginning the applicant was adamant,
quarrelsome, and whimsical.
It is further alleged by her that she has been treated with cruelty by the present applicant and his mother; even the applicant has not taken proper care of her during her pregnancy.
The sisters and mother of the applicant were instigating him.
The applicant has also made an attempt to abort her child without her consent and therefore, she constrained to lodge the report against him.
As per her contention, her marriage with the present applicant was second marriage.
She made every attempt to save marriage, but she was always insulted and humiliated by the present Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt applicant and his mother.
Even the applicant has not provided any expenses to her during her delivery.
After delivery also none turned up to see her and her child.

Despite she has intimated the present applicant to take her back after delivery, but he specifically stated that he would not come to take her and he has already filed an application for dissolution of marriage.

Thereafter, she along with her brother had gone to Nagpur, but she was not allowed to resume cohabitation with the present applicant and therefore, constrained to file an application for restitution of conjugal right as well as for maintenance.
6. The said application is resisted by the present applicant on the ground that after marriage, the behaviour of the respondent was not good.
She was not doing any household work and used to raise the quarrel with him.

She was abusing him as she was less educated compared to her and therefore,
he has always insulted by her.
She never shown love and affection to him.
Even his basic needs are not fulfilled by the respondent.

Though he had arranged a trip for her, but during the trip also she had raised a quarrel with the present applicant and his relatives which constrained him to file the petition for dissolution of marriage.
To give counterblast to the said petition for dissolution of marriage, the petition for restitution of conjugal rights and maintenance was filed by her.
Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt 7.
It is contention of the applicant that respondent is an educated lady serving as Assistant Professor and drawing handsome salary.

She is having sufficient means and to maintain herself and therefore,
the application for maintenance deserves to be rejected.

the learned Family Court dismissed the petition for dissolution of marriage and allowed the petition of respondent bearing No.A-136/2021 by which decree of Restitution of Conjugal Rights was passed and in Petition No.E-13/2021 maintenance at the rate of Rs.2,000/- each to the wife and son was granted from the date of application.
9. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the same, the present application is preferred by the applicant on the ground that the applicant has not sufficient means, his mother is dependent on him.

In view of that, the maintenance granted to the present respondent deserves to be quashed and set aside.
10. Heard learned counsel Ms. Vidya Umale for the applicant.
She submitted that as far as the refusal and neglect is concerned, except the evidence of the respondent, there is no evidence adduced by her, in support of her contention.
The evidence adduced by the present applicant sufficiently shows that she is having sufficient means to maintain herself.
She is able-bodied person and therefore, the maintenance granted by the Family Court deserves to be quashed and set aside.
She further submitted that the entire evidence of the respondent nowhere shows that it was the present applicant, who has refused and neglected her.

On the contrary, she has withdrawn herself from the company of the present applicant on that ground also she is not entitled for any maintenance.
11.
Before entering into the merits of the case, it is necessary to see the object behind the provision under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

The object of Section 125 of the Code is to provide a summary remedy to save dependents from Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt destitution and vagrancy, and thus to serve a social purpose apart from an independent obligation of the parties under their personal law.
Since the object is to prevent vagrancy or destitution by means of a summary remedy before a Magistrate, jurisdiction is preventive rather than remedial or punitive.
Foundation of an order under Section 125 is the neglect or refusal of the opposite party to maintain his wife, child or parents.
Refusal means a failure to maintain or denial of the obligation to maintain after demand.
"Neglect" on the other hand, means a default or omission to maintain, in the absence of a demand.
Neglect or refusal may be implied from the conduct of a party and need not be a formal refusal.

Refusal or neglect on the part of husband may be proved not only by express words, but also by his conduct.

sentences.text: In the light of the above object of the act, the evidence in the present case requires to be appreciated.
There is no dispute that marriage between the present applicant and respondent was performed on 19.11.2019.
It is also not disputed that prior to the marriage, the respondent was serving and after marriage also for some period she was serving.
First issue raised is that it was the present respondent, who has withdrawn herself from the company of the present applicant, and therefore, she is not entitled for any maintenance.
Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt 13.

On the contrary, it is contention of the respondent that she was ill-treated to the extent that she was not allowed to resume cohabitation and therefore, she constrained to take shelter at her parent's house.
The respondent entered into the witness box and reiterated the contentions as per her application for maintenance and restitution.
The sum and substance of her contention is that after marriage she resumed cohabitation.
At the relevant time, the applicant was residing along with his mother and one unmarried sister.

After marriage, she was treated well only for 15 days and thereafter, the mother and sister of the present applicant started insulting her by saying that she is not suitable in their house and she is not maintaining the standard.
Thus, she was mentally harassed by them.
It is further contended by her that they both were instigating her husband and her husband on their instigation, ill-treating her mentally.
The financial condition of her parents is not well.
Her father is suffering from Cancer and therefore, she could not disclose the said facts to her parents.
When she was pregnant at that time also her mother-in-law insisted her to leave her husband or live separately.
Thereafter, she went at her parent's house for the purpose of delivery.
After delivery also none turned up to see her or her child.

When she communicated with the applicant for taking her back after the delivery, the applicant informed her that he has already filed petition for dissolution of Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt marriage and he will not come to meet her.
Thus, the present applicant has refused to maintain her and has not made any provision for her livelihood as well as for the livelihood for her child.
During her cross-examination, it brought on record that the marriage was performed with the consent of both parties.
She further admits that her first marriage was dissolved by mutual consent and she has received the amount of Rs.5,00,000/- towards full and final settlement.

It further came in her cross-examination that she is educated than her husband,
but she denied that she humiliated and insulted her husband as he is less educated.

which is denied by her.
14. To counter the evidence of respondent, the applicant also adduced his evidence and stated that the respondent is well educated and after marriage her behaviour was not proper.
She was insulting him as he is less educated.
Despite he has made an attempt to make her happy by arranging the picnic, but during picnic also, she raised the quarrel.

His cross-examination further shows that the FIR is lodged against him under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
His cross-examination also shows that, this is a second marriage and he obtained the divorce from his first wife by consent by giving her an amount of Rs.2,50,000/-.
Thus, it is apparent that the marriage of the applicant as well as the respondent with each other is a second marriage.

15. In support of the contention, the applicant has examined Jyoti Prakash Kathale mother of the applicant, who also reiterated the contention that it was the respondent, who was not willing to cohabit with the applicant and used to raise quarrel with the present applicant and the other family members.
Admittedly, her evidence nowhere states any specific instances as far as raising quarrel by the respondent is concerned.
Admittedly, she is interested witness being the mother of the present applicant.
Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt 16.
Witness No.3 is examined by the applicant is Dr. Hemant Manikrao Baradkar, who stated that he is serving as Principal in Jagdamba Abhiyantriki Mahavidyalaya, Yavatmal.
He is acquainted with the respondent, who served as Associate Professor in the said College.
He specifically stated that her appointment for 11 months i.e. temporary in nature.
In the year 2021 to 2022, she was appointed for three months and then in the year 2022 to 2023 as well as in the year 2023 to 2024 she was appointed for 11 months.
During cross-examination, he admitted that the job of the respondent is private in nature and not permanent.
She can be removed from the service at any time.
17. On the basis of the said evidence, the applicant prayed that as she is independent, earning her livelihood and therefore, she is not entitled for any maintenance. Exh.52
the salary certificate of the respondent is brought on record which shows that in the month of June 2023 she drawn gross salary of Rs.54,500/-.

The statement of the present applicant towards assets and liabilities shows that he is not having any income and his mother pays him the amount of Rs.10,000/-.
18.

On appreciation of the evidence of the applicant as well as the respondent, as far as the aspect of the ill-treatment and cruelty is concerned, the expression 'cruelty' have been used in Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt relation to human conduct or human behaviour.
Cruelty thus is a course or conduct of one which adversely affects the others.

It may be mental or physical,
intentional or unintentional.
It is a question of fact and degree.
In the case of Samar Ghosh vs Jaya Ghosh (2007) 4 SCC 511, the Hon'ble Apex Court given certain illustrative examples where from inference of mental cruelty can be drawn.

The Hon'ble Apex Court reproduced some of the illustrations:
"(i) On consideration of complete matrimonial life of the parties, acute mental pain,
agony and suffering as would not make possible for the parties to live with each other, could come within the broad parameters of mental cruelty.

sentences.text: (ii) On comprehensive appraisal of the entire matrimonial life of the parties, if it becomes abundantly clear that situation is such that the wronged party cannot reasonably be asked to put up with such conduct and continue to live with other party.
(iii) Mental cruelty is a state of mind.

The feeling of deep anguish, disappointment,
frustration in one spouse caused by the conduct of other for a long time, may lead to mental cruelty.

(iv) Sustained reprehensible conduct, studied neglect, indifference or total departure from the normal standard of conjugal kindness causing injury to mental health or deriving sadistic pleasure can also amount to mental cruelty.
(v) The married life should be reviewed as a whole and a few isolated instances over a period of years will not amount to cruelty.

The ill-conduct must be persistent for a fairly lengthy period, where the relationship has deteriorated to an extent that because of the acts and behaviour of a spouse, the wronged party finds it Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt extremely difficult to live with the other party any longer, may amount to mental cruelty."
19. After adverting to material on record, it was established by the respondent that she was not treated well, as she was not respected in the family and she was consistently insulted and humiliated.
The fact that she resided along with the husband substantiates her allegations that her mother-in-law was asking her to live separately and therefore, she lived separately with the husband.
This fact is also admitted by the applicant which sufficiently shows that there was no comfort to her when she was residing along with the present applicant.
The ill-conduct for a long period is sufficient to attract the mental cruelty.

The aspect of not providing any provision for her after she went for delivery and not turning up when she delivered a child and directly notice was issued to her itself is sufficiently to show that the applicant was not intending to co-habit with her.
20. Torture or ill -treatment in the husband's house would be sufficient for refusal by the wife-claimant to live with her husband, even though husband may not be guilty personally.
Where a wife cannot hope to live with dignity with her husband she may refuse to live with him.
The offer must be bona fide and the same should not have been made with object to escaping the obligation to pay maintenance.
The burden that the wife is Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt refusing to live with him is to be discharged by the husband.
But once that is proved, it is for the wife to show that there are reasons for her living apart from the husband.
The object of Section 125 is to arm wife in difficulty with a cause of action to get maintenance from her erring husband.
Second proviso to Sub-section (3) of Section 125 is also relevant.

Even though a person offers to maintain his wife, with condition of her living with him and she refused to live with him, the Magistrate may consider ground of refusal as stated by wife-claimant and make an order under Section 126 of the Code not withstanding such offer, if he is satisfied that there is just ground for so doing.

sentences.text: Here in the present case, the applicant's conduct towards the respondent that she was consistently humiliated in the house therefore, she constrained to lodge a report under Section 498A of IPC, not turning to her when she delivered a child and thereafter issuing her notice for dissolution for marriage which sufficiently shows that there was refusal and neglect on the part of the present applicant.

22. It is vehemently submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the evidence on record sufficiently shows that she is educated lady and was serving as Associate Professor and getting income.

The evidence adduced by the applicant itself by way of examining the witness No.3 Dr.
Hemant Manikrao Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt Baradkar itself shows that it was not a permanent job, she was appointed for a temporary period and for that temporary period she had drawn the salary.
Thus, the evidence on record sufficiently shows that she has no sufficient means permanently for maintaining herself and her child.
Even accepting that she was earning some amount for her livelihood is not sufficient ground to deny her the maintenance.
In catena of decisions it is held that if the wife is earning, it cannot operate as a bar from being awarded maintenance by the husband.

The Courts have provided guidance on this issue in the case of Rajnesh vs Neha MANU/SC/0833/2020 by referring the judgment of Shailja Vs. Khobbanna, MANU/SC/0527/2017 the Apex Court has held that merely because the wife is capable of earning, it would not be a sufficient ground to reduce the maintenance awarded by the Family Court.
The Court has to determine whether the income of the wife is sufficient to enable her to maintain herself, in accordance with the lifestyle of her husband in the matrimonial home.
23. In Sunita Kachwaha Vs. Anil Kachwaha MANU/SC/0964/2014, wherein it is held that the wife had a postgraduate degree, and was employed as a teacher in Jabalpur.

entities.text: Sunita Kachwaha Vs. Anil Kachwaha MANU/SC/0964/2014,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The husband raised a contention that since the wife had sufficient income, she would not require financial assistance Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt from the husband.
The Apex Court repelled this contention, and held that merely because the wife was earning some income, it could not be a ground to reject her claim for maintenance.

24. It is further held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rajnesh vs Neha that an able-bodied husband must be presumed to be capable of earning sufficient money to maintain his wife and children, and cannot contend that he is not in a position to earn sufficiently to maintain his family.

The onus is on the husband to establish with necessary material that there are sufficient grounds to show that he is unable to maintain the family, and discharge his legal obligations for reasons beyond his control.
If the husband does not disclose the exact amount of his income, an adverse inference may be drawn by the Court.

25. In view of the above observation of the Hon'ble Apex Court, in the present case also the applicant has not disclosed his income and his contention is that his mother is providing him the amount of Rs.10,000/- is not sustainable.
Therefore, the learned Family Court has granted the maintenance at the rate of Rs.2,000/- per month on the basis of guesswork appears to be reasonable.

sentences.text: The law with respect to deciding the amount of permanent alimony is settled.

The status of the parties is a Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt significant factor, encompassing their social standing,
lifestyle, and financial background.
The reasonable needs of the wife and dependent children must be assessed, including costs for food, clothing, shelter, education, and medical expenses.
The applicant's educational and professional qualifications, as well as their employment history, play a crucial role in evaluating their potential for self-sufficiency.

If the applicant has any independent source of income or owns property, this will also be taken into account to determine if it is sufficient to maintain the same standard of living experienced during the marriage.

Additionally, the court considers whether the applicant had to sacrifice employment opportunities for family responsibilities, such as child-rearing or caring for elderly family members, which may have impacted their career prospects.

27. In the light of the above factors narrated by the Apex Court, if the facts of the present case are taken into consideration, admittedly, the learned Family Court has granted maintenance at the rate of Rs.2,000/- each to the respondent and her son which is meager amount.

Considering the prices of essential commodities are touching to the sky and the respondent has to incur the expenses towards the education and maintenance of the child as well as towards her maintenance and in that circumstances, the order passed by the learned Family Revn.254.2023.Judgment.odt Court granting maintenance is reasonable, just and proper one.
Therefore, the revision devoid of merits and liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, I proceed to pass following order:
ORDER The revision application is dismissed.
